findings.title: Migration crashes when no category matches embed_category
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row is returned. On the overwhelming majority of sites the `embed_category` site setting row does not exist (it is never saved unless changed), so the result set is empty and `[0]` is `nil`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil`. Every such site fails to migrate. Use a nil-safe fetch (e.g. `rows.first && rows.first['id'].to_i`) before falling back to uncategorized.

findings.title: Unescaped host value interpolated into INSERT statement
findings.body: The host string comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting and is interpolated directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. A host containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacter) breaks the statement or allows SQL injection during migration. Use `quote(h)` / a parameterized insert. Additionally the raw value is not stripped of `http://`/paths like `EmbeddableHost`'s before_validation does, so migrated rows will not match `record_for_host` lookups and embedding will silently break after upgrade.

findings.title: create_table force: true in migration can drop an existing table
findings.body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS first. If the migration is re-run or the table already exists for any reason, existing embeddable host rows are destroyed without warning. Also, because the migration uses `execute` inside `change` (including a destructive `DELETE FROM site_settings`), it is not reversible; it should be split into `up`/`down`.

findings.title: has_many with embed: :ids does not include the host objects, admin page will show no hosts
findings.body: `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids` serializes only `embeddable_host_ids` and does not sideload the actual `embeddable_hosts` array. The Ember store's `_hydrateEmbedded` looks up the ids in `root['embeddable_hosts']`, which is absent, so hydration yields `undefined` entries and the embedding admin template renders empty/broken rows. Use `embed: :ids, include: true` (or sideload the collection explicitly).

findings.title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown id
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing/deleted record; `save_host(nil)` then calls `host.host =` and `destroy` on nil, producing a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `find`).

findings.title: before_validation raises on nil host instead of failing validation
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in `before_validation`. Creating/saving an `EmbeddableHost` with a nil host (e.g. an admin submitting a blank host — the controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly) raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, returning a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?` and add `validates_presence_of :host`.

findings.title: Host lookup is not case-insensitive on the input side
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value derived from the referer/URL. A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/page` yields `uri.host == "EvilTrout.com"`, which never matches the lowercased column, so legitimate embeds are rejected with 'invalid referer host'. Pass `host.downcase`.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint or index on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two `embeddable_hosts` rows with the same host (the model has no uniqueness validation and the migration adds no unique index). `record_for_host` then silently picks an arbitrary row, making the category used for embedded topics nondeterministic. Add a uniqueness validation and a unique index on `lower(host)`.

findings.title: PostCreator `category:` option now receives an id instead of a name
findings.body: The previous code passed `category: SiteSetting.embed_category`, a category name string; the new code passes `eh.try(:category_id)`, an integer. If PostCreator's `category` option is resolved by name, the embedded topic will land in no/uncategorized category instead of the configured one. Verify PostCreator's contract and pass `category_id` (or the name) accordingly — the added spec only asserts equality when the fabricated host's category happens to resolve.

findings.title: Plural embedded hydration assumes array and keeps undefined entries
findings.body: `obj[k].map(...)` is called without checking that `obj[k]` is an array; any attribute whose name matches `(.+)_ids$` but holds null/a scalar throws a TypeError during hydration. Additionally, unlike the singular branch, the plural branch deletes the original `_ids` key unconditionally and stores entries that may be `undefined` when a sub-object is not sideloaded, silently producing a collection of undefined models (which is exactly what happens with the embedding payload).

findings.title: replace('_','-') only converts the first underscore
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` without the `g` flag replaces only the first underscore, so a future admin model type with two or more underscores (e.g. `site_customization_thing`) would not match an entry in ADMIN_MODELS and would be requested from the non-admin path. Use `.replace(/_/g, '-')`.

findings.title: Embedding#update is a no-op
findings.body: `update` performs no state change but returns 200 with the serialized embedding, and the client's `saveChanges` calls `embedding.update({})`. Any future/implied 'save settings' action on this page silently does nothing, which is misleading to callers. Either implement the update or drop the route and the client action.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped between category and embeddable_host files
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. The file names no longer describe their contents, which will confuse anyone looking for `Fabricate(:category)` or `Fabricate(:private_category)`. Swap the contents.

findings.title: No request specs for the new embeddable hosts endpoints
findings.body: The only assertion is that the controller subclasses Admin::AdminController. The new create/update/destroy actions (including the nil-record paths and the uncategorized-category fallback) and the embedding show/update endpoints are untested, so regressions such as the 500 on a missing id would not be caught.
